task.description: RE-VALIDATION after rework: CODE-DESIGNER rewrote Section 6 (previously real Elixir/Ecto code) into prose algorithm steps matching req024-event-type-registry.md Section 4.4's style -- re-run the full checklist fresh, in particular re-check 'no implementation code present' specifically against the new Section 6 (grep for repo., Ecto.Multi., Ecto.Query, 'with ... do', 'case ... do', on_conflict:, conflict_target:, prefix:, lock:, and %{ map-literal construction yourself; do not trust CODE-DESIGNER's self-report that it's clean). Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md. CODE-DESIGNER flagged two open questions (OQ-1, OQ-5) as issues in its handoff -- ORCH already independently checked OQ-1 against docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md's Addendum (2026-08-17): the addendum's own text explicitly scopes the tenant_id-derivation requirement to 'events/events_archive/instance_projections (REQ-023's schema, REQ-025's writer) and process_definitions (REQ-027's schema, REQ-030's writer)' -- instance_sequence and event_idempotency are not named and, confirmed directly against lib/letflow/event_store/instance_sequence.ex and idempotency_record.ex, genuinely have no tenant_id column at all. Verify this independently yourself (read the addendum and both schema files directly) and confirm the design's OQ-1 resolution (isolation for those two tables via :prefix schema boundary, not a column; REQ-025's AC6 wording read in light of the decision record rather than literally) is correct -- this is not a design gap, it's the design correctly reconciling an imprecisely-worded acceptance criterion against an already-settled decision record. OQ-5 (instance_projections insert-if-absent at first append) is a genuine scope-interpretation judgment call against REQ-023's EE-01/S3 deferral language -- confirm the design states it explicitly (not silently) and flag it prominently for REVIEWER's Step 2d attention (do not resolve it yourself, that's not this gate's job, but do not let it pass as if unremarkable either).
acceptance_criteria: appending to a terminated instance (status CANCELLED or COMPLETED in instance_projections) returns an error and writes zero rows across all five involved tables, demonstrated by an actual test or iex session against a real Postgres, not just described

two concurrent appends to the same instance_id never receive the same sequence_number -- demonstrated with an actual concurrent test (e.g. Task.async_stream racing two appends) or, if concurrency can't be exercised in this environment, the FOR UPDATE-equivalent locking code path is cited explicitly
appending twice with the same idempotency_key returns is_duplicate: true on the second call and does not insert a second events row, verified against the idempotency sidecar table REQ-023 defines
a payload that fails REQ-024's validate_payload/2 results in zero rows written to events, instance_sequence, or instance_projections -- no partial state
a payload over 4096 bytes is split into events.payload's $ref pointer form plus an event_payload_store row, verified by reading both rows back after append

every row append/1(2) writes (events, instance_sequence, instance_projections, the idempotency sidecar) has tenant_id equal to the tenant whose schema the write targeted, derived internally -- not equal to a caller-supplied tenant_id when the two are deliberately made to disagree in a test, which must fail loudly (not silently attribute to the wrong tenant) rather than succeed

Read lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md in full (871 lines, not CODE-DESIGNER's summary), the WF-02 Step 1b checklist (.claude/agents/code-design-validator.md, docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 1b), docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-025 entry (1042-1100), the 0003 addendum's 2026-08-17 section in full (lines 326-396), and both lib/letflow/event_store/instance_sequence.ex and idempotency_record.ex directly. Ran the full checklist fresh against all six acceptance criteria, not just the previously-failed item.

CHECK 2e (no implementation code present) -- the item that failed last round -- now PASSES. Grepped the file directly (not trusting CODE-DESIGNER's self-report) for repo. (0 hits), Ecto.Multi. (2 hits, both prose: line 365 names what the design is NOT doing, line 458 is a generic schematic 'Ecto.Multi.new() |> Multi.run(...) |> ...' using ellipsis placeholders inside a sentence that explicitly disclaims literalness -- 'described here by what it does rather than by its literal call form'), Ecto.Query (1 hit, a prose citation of security-invariants.md's INV-7 guidance, not code), 'with ... do' (0 hits), 'case ... do' (0 hits), on_conflict: (3 hits, all prose citations naming an existing shipped idiom by name -- e.g. 'reuses the exact re-select after on_conflict: :nothing idiom already shipped in tenant_provisioning.ex:315-338' -- never as a literal keyword argument inside a real function call in this doc), conflict_target: (0 hits -- present in the prior failing version, now removed), prefix: (hits confined to the @spec in 5.1, a section header phrase, the moduledoc requirement, and the cross-module dependency table -- none inside a literal Ecto call with real arguments in the 6.2.x algorithm blocks), lock: (0 hits -- the prior version's literal lock: "FOR UPDATE" Ecto option is gone, replaced by prose 'acquiring an exclusive row lock'), %{ (4 hits: three inside Section 5.2/5.4's @type specs -- legitimate type-shape notation, explicitly allowed by this gate's own instructions -- and one inline `attrs[:metadata] || %{}` default-value expression in P3, a minor real-syntax fragment consistent with the approved req024 Section 4.4 reference's own style of blending prose with real function-call/bracket-access syntax, e.g. req024's `collect(join_pointer(pointer, name), value[name], subschema)`). Also grepped for def /defmodule/Multi.run(/Multi.insert(/Multi.update(/Repo.insert(/Repo.update_all(/Repo.one(/from( as a second pass -- zero hits anywhere in the file. Sections 6.1 P5/P6, 6.2.2-6.2.6 (M2-M6), and 6.3 -- the specific sections that failed last round with near-literal Elixir/Ecto function bodies -- are now entirely prose/structured-English algorithm description (e.g. M2's locking protocol is now 'Attempt to insert a fresh instance_sequence row... configured as an atomic insert-or-ignore keyed on instance_id... Read the instance_sequence row back, acquiring an exclusive row lock...' with no repo.insert/on_conflict:/conflict_target:/prefix:/lock: literal call), matching req024-event-type-registry.md Section 4.4's cited style (English conditionals, no def/do/end, no real Ecto option syntax chained into a working pipeline).

CHECK 2a (design element per AC, no TBD/deferral) -- PASS. Grepped for TBD|to be determined|to be decided|to be implemented later|not yet specified|left as an exercise -- zero matches anywhere in the file. Every AC maps to a concrete design element in Section 11's traceability table (AC1->6.2.1 M1 + INV-AP-7; AC2->6.2.2's locking protocol + INV-AP-5; AC3->6.2.3 M3 + 6.3's duplicate branch + INV-AP-6; AC4->6.1 P4 running entirely pre-transaction + INV-AP-4; AC5->6.1 P5 + 6.2.4 M4 + 6.2.5 M5 + INV-AP-8; AC6->Section 3's no-tenant_id-accepted design + Section 4's derivation function + INV-AP-1/2/9, with OQ-1 flagging the requirement-text/shipped-schema mismatch explicitly rather than silently narrowing it).

CHECK 2b (function signatures fully specified) -- PASS. Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 (Section 4) has a full @spec with both success and error return shapes. Letflow.EventStore.append/2 (Section 5.1) has a full @spec, attrs shape (5.2), a 20-plus-variant tagged error union (5.3), and result shape (5.4).

CHECK 2c (error handling shape stated) -- PASS. Section 5.3's append_error() union tags every failure mode by name ({:error, atom} or {:error, {atom, detail}} throughout), no implicit/untyped error path; each variant is annotated with which requirement-named case or invariant it satisfies.

CHECK 2d (cross-module dependencies listed) -- PASS. Section 10 lists all six dependencies (TenantProvisioning, Registry, the five REQ-023 schema modules, Repo, and the two forward-looking consumers REQ-026/REQ-030) with direction and nature stated for each.

OQ-1 independently re-verified against source (not trusted from CODE-DESIGNER's or ORCH's characterization): read the 0003 addendum's 2026-08-17 section directly (lines 326-396) -- its own text names exactly 'events/events_archive/instance_projections (REQ-023's schema, REQ-025's writer) and process_definitions (REQ-027's schema, REQ-030's writer)' as the tables the tenant_id-derivation decision covers (lines 339-341); instance_sequence and event_idempotency are not named. Read lib/letflow/event_store/instance_sequence.ex directly: schema fields are only :next_seq (plus :instance_id primary key) -- no tenant_id field anywhere in the schema block (lines 31-34). Read lib/letflow/event_store/idempotency_record.ex directly: schema fields are :idempotency_key, :event_id, :event_created_at, timestamps -- no tenant_id field anywhere (lines 67-74). Both confirmed genuinely absent at the Ecto-schema level. REQ-025's own requirement description (docs/requirements.yaml 1085-1087) asserts all four tables carry a NOT NULL tenant_id column with no default -- that is the imprecise wording the addendum and shipped schema override. The design's resolution (INV-AP-9: isolation for the two column-less tables is enforced by the :prefix schema boundary, not a column; OQ-1 flagged prominently in Section 9 with a concrete adapted-test instruction for TEST-DESIGNER, and explicitly routed to REVIEWER as 'a requirement-text/shipped-schema mismatch, not resolved unilaterally by silently editing docs/requirements.yaml') is correct and is not itself a design gap.

OQ-5 confirmed stated explicitly, not silently resolved or silently dropped: Section 9 labels it 'MAJOR -- a real scope-boundary judgment call, not a minor detail,' explains the interpretive reasoning (M6 creating the bare instance_projections row vs. REQ-023's EE-01/S3 deferral of 'meaningful population'), and explicitly states 'REVIEWER should explicitly confirm this reading rather than this design's own judgment call standing unchallenged' -- prominently flagged for REVIEWER's Step 2d attention, not resolved by this gate.

Net: all five checklist items (2a-2e) pass. No partial-credit override needed since nothing failed. Design is unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to build from without inventing behavior.
